speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your skin lesions for potential oncologic issues. Can you describe the primary lesion in detail, including its size, shape, color, and any changes over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma

The clinical presentation of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penis in a 62-year-old male with a significant smoking history and history of failed syphilis treatment is highly suggestive of Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The concurrent lesion on the finger raises suspicion for field cancerization or a second primary tumor. I need to confirm the nature of these lesions before proceeding to biopsy. Can you confirm if these lesions are painful or bleeding, and have you noticed any lymph node swelling in the groin or armpit areas?
